title: [AUG-74] RCA: Color utility schema not applied to element-level audit — page titles missed
why_we_need_this: During AUG-71 (Major FE audit), the color utility schema section was marked "Compliant" after verifying only structural rules (no #fff backgrounds, no bright/neon green, correct status colors). The agent never checked whether EACH visible element uses the correct priority-based color treatment per the schema — e.g. whether page titles use top/high-priority color (var(--accent)) vs low-priority body text color (var(--text-primary)). The ".circuit-title" heading "New Transcription" uses var(--text-primary), which is low-priority styling for what is the main page heading. This was missed because the color audit checked palette-level constraints (forbidden values) but not semantic-level constraints (is each element's color appropriate for its importance level).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Root cause documented: the color audit checked CSS-level "don't use X" rules but skipped the semantic "use Y for this importance level" rules from the Color Utility Schema section

2. Prevention rule: when auditing color compliance, the agent must perform TWO passes:
   - Pass 1 (palette constraints): forbidden values, missing dark overrides, hardcoded vs token usage
   - Pass 2 (semantic compliance): for every visible text element and button, verify its color treatment matches its importance level per the Color Utility Schema (top → green filled/green text, high → yellow filled/green bold text, normal → outline, low → plain text, situational → red only)

3. The semantic pass must enumerate each page's visible elements and classify them by importance level, then verify the CSS matches. Elements to check: page titles, section titles, button labels, status text, metadata, action labels, modal titles

4. Apply retroactively: audit all page titles, section titles, and primary headings in App.css against the Color Utility Schema and fix any that use the wrong priority color
